focus: Finishing Grade 12 while building, researching, and following questions that genuinely interest me.

sections.title: Right Now
items: Finishing Grade 12 and strengthening my foundations in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and computer science.
Preparing seriously for competitive examinations while trying to become better at solving unfamiliar problems rather than just completing more questions.
Building a habit of turning curiosity into experiments, projects, and actual research.

sections.title: Building
items: MechLang — a domain-specific language for representing and rendering organic reaction mechanisms.
FocusVector — a privacy-conscious browser extension exploring whether observable reading behavior can be used to estimate attention drift.
This website — an evolving record of my projects, research, writing, experiments, and ideas.

sections.title: Research
items: Investigating why chemistry textbooks report apparently identical electron gain enthalpies for argon and krypton.
Tracing the historical origin of the reported values through primary literature.
Using scattering theory to investigate whether there is a deeper physical explanation behind the observation.

sections.title: Thinking About
items: How to tell whether a research question is genuinely open or simply unfamiliar.
How computational tools can help investigate scientific questions without replacing physical reasoning.
Why seemingly simple observations sometimes hide surprisingly deep explanations.
How to turn curiosity into disciplined, reproducible work.
